links.outcome: Clinical thinking/logic score of generated protocol sections, RAG vs off-the-shelf GPT-4
links.effect: RAG-augmented LLM scored about twice as high on clinical thinking and logic; eligibility criteria ~33% to ~86%, endpoints ~50% to ~73%; only this dimension survived Bonferroni correction.
links.quote: However, the RAG-augmented LLM substantially outperforms the off-the-shelf LLM in terms of clinical thinking and logic , where the output of the RAG-augmented LLM scores approximately twice as high as the off-the-shelf LLM.

links.outcome: Presence and correctness of cited references in generated protocol text
links.effect: Off-the-shelf GPT-4 does not natively source references so transparency could not be scored; RAG-augmented LLM references were correct and appropriate nearly 80% of the time.
links.quote: Regarding transparency and references , the RAG-augmented LLM (by design) includes references, which we show to be correct and appropriate nearly 80% of the time.

links.outcome: Adherence of off-the-shelf LLM recommendations to current regulatory guidance
links.effect: Off-the-shelf LLM scored just over 40% on clinical thinking and logic; example excluded HIV, diabetes, liver and kidney disease patients from a TB trial contrary to FDA guidance.
links.quote: However, for clinical thinking and logic , the off-the-shelf LLM scores poorly (assessment score just over 40%), meaning that recommendations from the off-the-shelf LLM often do not follow the latest regulatory guidance or contain other errors.
